blocks.text:
The next four days have no compulsory transfers or excursions.

At Nannai Muro Alto, you can head to the beach in the morning, wait for low tide and swim behind the reef wall. There are few strong waves here, the water is warm, and the pale seabed is clearly visible even farther from shore.

For a change of scene, the resort centre offers trips on **jangadas**, local flat rafts, to the natural pools. At low tide, pockets of clear water remain between the reefs, with small fish that are easy to watch through a snorkelling mask.

Diving and buggy rides along the coast are also available.

You can also spend these days without extra trips: relax by the pool, walk around Muro Alto, and return to the sea in the morning and evening when the sand is cooler. After the busy programme in Rio, Iguazu and Bonito, this part of the trip offers a few quiet days without constantly changing hotels.
